hero.lead: I build AI systems that can show where an answer came from.

paragraphs: I started with datasets and Flutter screens. Working on both gave me a habit I still use. I follow an input all the way to the person who gets the result. In a support assistant, that means opening the source FAQ behind a reply. In a recommendation engine, it means checking why a product reached the top.

I’m based in Noida. My engineering work spans search, document extraction, recommendations, and computer vision. I currently work in AI consulting, bringing those engineering habits to conversations with business users.

projects.title: PawSupport
projects.intro: A pet-care assistant that traces a customer’s question back to an approved FAQ.
paragraphs: Customers can ask about the same policy in different words. I built a router that tries an exact FAQ match, a semantic match, and an alias lookup. When it finds a suitable FAQ, the language model can rephrase the approved answer.

To check the router, I used a labeled offline test set. Each answerable example points to its expected FAQ identifier. The evaluation can catch a persuasive reply that came from the wrong policy. Other examples check whether the system declines a question outside its scope.

projects.title: SupportPilot
projects.intro: A support API with an explicit decision about when it has enough evidence to answer.
paragraphs: A request enters through FastAPI. A rule-based agent labels the intent, and ChromaDB returns three candidate FAQs. The retrieval agent turns the closest result’s cosine distance into a score and checks it against a threshold.

A strong match supplies context for the language model. A weak match takes a fixed fallback path and skips the generation call. Separating retrieval from response generation makes that decision easy to trace in the code.

projects.title: Abyssal Observatory
projects.intro: The Django application behind this portfolio, with an animated GitHub profile and a static edition for GitHub Pages.
paragraphs: Every project has its own Django route. The homepage lists the studies and opens them directly. A single structured content file supplies the project summaries and detail pages.

A Django management command renders the same routes and gathers the artwork into a portable static site. The character’s breathing loops automatically, while scroll lighting and other background effects are adjusted for visitors who prefer reduced motion.

projects.title: Veterinary document extraction
projects.intro: A FastAPI service that turns veterinary PDFs into a workbook with separate record types.
paragraphs: A veterinary document can hold a pet’s details, its treatment, and its next follow-up in the same file. I built a service that extracts those records, validates the fields, and writes each record type to its own Excel sheet. The structure lets a reviewer inspect a follow-up without reading the whole PDF again.

projects.title: Product recommendations
projects.intro: A purchase-history recommender that distinguishes repeat demand from one unusually large order.
paragraphs: I used cosine similarity to find customers with similar purchase histories, then collected products their peers had bought. Ranking by quantity gave occasional bulk purchases too much influence. I switched the ranking signal to order frequency and excluded anything the customer had already purchased.

projects.title: Pet breed identification
projects.intro: An image API that returns an explicit unknown result when the model has low confidence.
paragraphs: I prototyped a service that accepts a pet photo and asks GPT-4o Vision for a structured prediction. I checked the image input, validated the model’s JSON, and mapped low reported confidence to an unknown result. A caller can handle that outcome directly instead of treating every prediction as a definite breed.

projects.title: Student & Recruiter Job Portal
projects.intro: A two-sided Flutter app for browsing openings, posting jobs or internships, and reviewing applications.
paragraphs: A student can move from search to an opening and start an application. A separate recruiter flow collects the role, skills, and screening questions for a job or internship posting. Recruiters can also open a list of applicants to review.

This repository hosts a shared app snapshot originally committed by an109. Its dependency configuration connects the screens to repositories, use cases, and BLoCs. Listings and applications need access to the configured backend.

projects.title: Flutter Job Discovery
projects.intro: A related job-portal snapshot focused on skills onboarding, search filters, and the candidate’s application flow.
paragraphs: The candidate’s signup flow groups skills and subskills by domain. When looking for a role, the candidate can set location and work-experience filters, then open the job details.

This snapshot shares code with the Student & Recruiter Job Portal. Its candidate flow exposes a useful state transition: the job details screen listens for the application result while a dedicated BLoC handles the submission event. Live listings and submissions depend on the configured backend.

projects.title: Terminal Tic-Tac-Toe
projects.intro: A standard-library Python game that lets a human play tic-tac-toe against a computer in the terminal.
paragraphs: Squares are numbered from one to nine. The human plays X and chooses an available square. The computer plays O by choosing randomly from the spaces still open.
The game checks rows, columns, and diagonals to detect a win and recognizes a draw when the board fills. The board, opponent logic, and turn loop are small enough to follow in one Python file.
